summary: Retest of Backup/Restore CSS overlap fix and backend restore error-path. Focus scope from main agent honored (no full pytest re-run). Confirmed: (1) element at the visual center of 'Restore now' is now the <button data-testid=restore-submit-button> itself (not the .dropzone label), a real Playwright .click() with NO force=True fires the form submit; (2) success banner data-testid='backup-message' renders with text 'Restore complete · 20 transactions, 2 accounts, 3 sites available.'; (3) 'Download backup ZIP' link and 'Delete sample data' button remain visible and enabled; (4) curl GET /api/backup → 200 (returns ZIP), curl POST /api/restore with valid ZIP → 200 with {restored:true,transactions:20,accounts:2,sites:3}, curl POST /api/restore with non-ZIP text file → 400 with clean detail 'Uploaded file is not a valid backup ZIP' (no 500). All five review-request items pass.
critical_code_review_comments: CSS fix using .backup-card flex-column + .backup-card>button {align-self:flex-start; position:relative; z-index:1} is correct and minimal; button now sits outside the dropzone label's stacking area.

server.py /api/restore now correctly funnels generic extraction errors to HTTP 400 via 'except Exception as exc: raise HTTPException(400, ...)' after BadZipFile and after re-raising HTTPException — order is right.
App.js still uses default axios error handling; that's fine here. Explicit type='submit' added to restore button is a small hardening win.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Restore now clickable without force; banner shown; other buttons intact)

seed_data_creation: None — used the app's existing demo seed via /api/backup then restored the same ZIP.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration_3 flagged the .dropzone label overlapping the Restore now submit button on /backup. Iteration_4 verifies the fix: elementFromPoint at the button center now returns the BUTTON (data-testid=restore-submit-button), not the label. Backend regression for non-ZIP upload now returns 400 (previously 500 risk). No open issues on Backup page.
rca of the issue: Previous overlap caused by .dropzone (a <label>) expanding and its absolutely-positioned <input> covering the sibling submit <button>. Fixed by making .backup-card a flex-column with the button given align-self:flex-start, position:relative, z-index:1, plus constrained .dropzone padding/min-height so it no longer overflows. Verified via document.elementFromPoint at button center.
